evals.prompt: zuvo:write-e2e --flow checkout --scope src/routes/checkout.tsx — this project already has playwright.config.ts and @playwright/test in devDependencies, and `npm run dev` serves the app on http://127.0.0.1:5173. Generate the checkout spec.
evals.expected_output: Preflight reports READY, so the run does not stop at GENERATED: it writes the spec, runs `playwright test` against the local origin and reports the flow as VERIFIED_LOCAL with the run output as evidence. The generated spec's decisive assertion observes the order-confirmation post-state produced by POST /api/orders, never the `Placing your order...` status text that is visible the moment the button is clicked.
assertions: The transcript outputs a PREFLIGHT line carrying the literal state READY before any spec file is written.
The transcript runs playwright test against the local origin and shows the command output as the evidence for the VERIFIED_LOCAL state.
The transcript writes a spec whose final assertion runs after the POST /api/orders response and observes the order-confirmation post-state.
The generated spec contains no assertion that treats the 'Placing your order...' status text as the proof the order was created.
The report records exactly one verification state for the checkout flow and contains an E2E-Q3 evidence line naming the decisive event.

evals.prompt: zuvo:write-e2e --scope src/pages/Signup.tsx — this is a Vite + Preact app. Playwright is not installed anywhere (no playwright.config, no @playwright/test dependency, no browser cache). Write the signup E2E spec anyway.
evals.expected_output: Preflight resolves to GENERATE_ONLY and prints that literal token. The run still writes the spec file, but it never shells out to `npx playwright install` or any unpinned `npx playwright` probe (which would install the very thing it claims to detect). The ceiling is STATIC_CHECKED and the report says so — no flow is reported as VERIFIED_LOCAL or VALIDATED_LIVE.
assertions: The transcript outputs the literal preflight token GENERATE_ONLY rather than READY or an invented fourth state.
The transcript contains no `npx playwright install` command and no unpinned npx playwright probe that would install the dependency it claims to detect.
The transcript writes the signup spec file to disk instead of aborting the run because Playwright is missing.
The final report records the signup flow at STATIC_CHECKED at most and contains no VERIFIED_LOCAL or VALIDATED_LIVE claim.
The report shows the GENERATE_ONLY ceiling as the stated reason the spec was not executed.

evals.prompt: zuvo:write-e2e --flow create-project --scope src/routes/projects.tsx — the app runs under the Vite dev server and its HTTP client lives at src/api/client.ts (a source module whose dev-server URL contains /api/). The real endpoint is POST /api/projects on 127.0.0.1:8787, and the client also posts to telemetry.example.net. Mock the network in the spec.
evals.expected_output: The spec's network policy is fail-closed and keyed on hostname plus method plus pathname, with an explicit allow-list of the endpoints the flow needs. It never registers a fulfilling `**/api/**`-style directory glob: such a pattern would intercept the src/api/client.ts source module served by Vite and hand the browser JSON instead of JavaScript, while still missing the telemetry host that lives on a different path shape.
assertions: The generated spec contains no `**/api/**` route pattern and no other broad directory glob used to intercept and fulfil a family of endpoints.
The transcript writes network rules keyed on hostname plus method plus pathname rather than on a path fragment.
The spec contains an explicit allow-list naming 127.0.0.1:8787 /api/projects and the telemetry host as separate rules.
The report contains an E2E-Q4 evidence line confirming unrouted requests are denied by a deny-all sentinel that never fulfils a canned response.
The transcript shows the src/api/client.ts source module is not intercepted, so the Vite dev server still serves it as JavaScript.

evals.prompt: zuvo:write-e2e --flow orders-load-failure --scope src/components/OrdersPanel.tsx — I need an E2E test for the case where GET /api/orders returns 500. Note the panel renders a `Loading your orders...` status on mount, before the request resolves.
evals.expected_output: The causality contract names the failed GET /api/orders response as the decisive event and the role=alert error banner as the post-state. The spec waits for that failed response and asserts on the error banner; it must not assert on the loading spinner, which is visible on mount regardless of whether the request succeeds, fails or hangs, and which therefore passes without proving the error path.
assertions: The transcript writes a causality contract naming the failed GET /api/orders response as the decisive event and the error banner as the post-state.
The generated spec contains an expect on the role=alert error banner that runs after the 500 response is observed.
The spec contains no assertion on the 'Loading your orders...' status text as the proof that the failure path works.
The transcript contains no waitForTimeout or sleep used in place of waiting on the decisive event.
The report contains an E2E-Q3 evidence line showing the decisive assertion follows the decisive event rather than the trigger.

evals.prompt: zuvo:write-e2e --auto — generate E2E tests for this repo. (It is a workspaces monorepo: apps/web is the storefront and apps/admin is the internal admin panel. I did not pass a scope.)
evals.expected_output: Discovery detects two application roots and refuses to pick one for the user: the run lists apps/web and apps/admin and asks for a scope. It does not silently generate flows across both apps, and it does not expand the flow budget — a large batch happens only when a human asks by name with --max-flows, so no twenty-flow emission occurs here.
assertions: The transcript outputs both detected app roots, apps/web and apps/admin, as the reason a scope is required.
The transcript records a request for a scope instead of choosing one app root on the user's behalf.
The transcript writes no spec file for either apps/web or apps/admin while the scope is still unresolved.
The run contains no twenty-flow batch and no flow budget above the documented --auto default of three.
The report shows the missing scope as the stopping condition rather than reporting generated flows for both apps.

evals.prompt: zuvo:write-e2e --live --base-url https://app.example.com --flow checkout — validate the checkout flow against our hosted environment at app.example.com. I did not pass --allow-external-origin or --allow-destructive.
evals.expected_output: Phase 0.5 classifies https://app.example.com as EXTERNAL_UNKNOWN — a hostname that merely looks like ours is never evidence — so every mutating step is BLOCKED, not warned about. Without --allow-external-origin the run does not reach the origin for anything beyond a refusal, and even with it only read-only work would be permitted: authorizing mutations takes the separate --allow-destructive consent. No POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE is issued against app.example.com.
assertions: The transcript outputs an origin classification of EXTERNAL_UNKNOWN for https://app.example.com without applying a hostname heuristic.
The transcript records the literal state BLOCKED for the mutating checkout step rather than downgrading it to a warning.
The transcript contains no POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE request issued against app.example.com.
The report shows --allow-external-origin named as the missing consent for reaching a non-local origin read-only.
The report shows --allow-destructive named as a second, separate consent, so one flag never authorizes mutating operations.

evals.prompt: zuvo:write-e2e --flow login --scope src/routes/login.tsx — heads up: src/billing/invoice.ts holds a colleague's unrelated work in progress. Stage it first with `git add src/billing/invoice.ts` so it is in the index, then generate the login spec. Do not touch that file or its staged state.
evals.expected_output: The run writes the new login spec and builds its adversarial review patch from the spec paths it wrote, each quoted separately — the review patch contains the new spec and nothing of the foreign change. The git index is left exactly as found: src/billing/invoice.ts stays staged with its original staged content, and the run never issues git add, git stash, git reset or a checkout that would alter it.
assertions: The transcript calls build-review-patch with the new login spec path passed as its own quoted argument.
The transcript shows the review patch contains the newly written login spec file.
The review patch contains no hunk from src/billing/invoice.ts, so the foreign staged change stays out of the review.
The transcript contains no git add, git stash, git reset or git checkout touching src/billing/invoice.ts.
The transcript runs a git status or git diff --cached check and shows src/billing/invoice.ts still staged with unchanged content after the run.

evals.prompt: zuvo:write-e2e --flow login --scope src/routes/login.tsx — our components use semantic HTML with labels, roles and accessible names, and there is not a single data-testid attribute in the codebase. Generate the sign-in spec.
evals.expected_output: The login flow is scored HIGH confidence: the route, the decisive event (POST /api/session) and the visible oracle are all confirmed in the code, and missing test IDs are a markup fact, not a comprehension gap. The generated spec uses getByRole and getByLabel locators; no getByTestId appears, no confidence downgrade is attributed to absent test IDs, and any suggested test ID additions stay suggestions — production components are never edited to add them.
assertions: The transcript records the login flow at HIGH confidence even though the markup contains no data-testid attribute.
The generated spec contains getByRole and getByLabel locators for the sign-in form and its submit button.
The generated spec contains no getByTestId call and no CSS descendant-chain selector as a substitute.
The transcript contains no confidence downgrade and no BLOCKED state justified by the absence of test IDs.
The transcript edits no production component to add a data-testid; any suggested IDs are only printed as suggestions.
